title: Blackwell (SM100) Architecture Features for CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Use TMEM for large accumulators to reduce register pressure
Adopt FP6/FP4 for ultra-low precision inference
Leverage 2-CTA instructions for larger cooperative tiles
Use block-scaled formats for better quantization accuracy
constraints: Documentation may be incomplete; check NVIDIA updates
CuTe Python DSL support is evolving; some features may be C++ only initially
compressed_summary: The Blackwell (SM100) architecture introduces significant advancements for AI workloads, including 5th generation Tensor Cores with enhanced support for FP4, FP6, and FP8, a new memory hierarchy level called Tensor Memory (TMEM), and 2-CTA instructions for cross-block cooperation. Key features include block-scaled formats for improved quantization accuracy and enhanced TMA with direct TMEM support. The B200 GPU features approximately 208 SMs, over 30,000 CUDA cores, and 832+ Tensor Cores, with a memory bandwidth of 8 TB/s. Practical patterns for CuTe DSL users include utilizing TMEM for large accumulators to reduce register pressure, adopting FP6/FP4 for ultra-low precision inference, leveraging 2-CTA instructions for processing larger tiles efficiently, and using block-scaled formats for better quantization accuracy. Constraints include the evolving nature of Blackwell support, incomplete documentation, and limited availability of B100/B200 GPUs. Migration from Hopper to Blackwell is facilitated by the compatibility of existing Hopper code, with recommendations to incorporate TMEM usage and explore FP4/FP6 for new workloads. Blackwell is ideal for large model training, extreme quantization inference, and memory-bound workloads, offering significant performance improvements over previous architectures.
